'''Richard Vincent Kadison''' (July 25, 1925 – August 22, 2018)<ref name="guysal"/> was an American mathematician known for his contributions to the study of [[operator algebra]]s.

==Career==
Born in New York City in 1925,<ref name="guysal">{{cite web |title=In Memoriam, University of Pennsylvania, Department of Mathematics |url=https://www.math.upenn.edu/about/department-history/in-memoriam|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624130320/https://www.math.upenn.edu/about/department-history/in-memoriam|archive-date=2021-06-24|url-status=dead |publisher=University of Pennsylvania}}</ref><ref name="loc">{{cite web|title=Library of Congress Name Authority File|url=http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n82090181.html|publisher=Library of Congress}}</ref> Kadison was a Gustave C. Kuemmerle Professor in the Department of Mathematics of the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name="penn">[http://www.math.upenn.edu/History/recog/kadison.html Richard Kadison wins 1999 AMS Steele Prize.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100619052545/http://www.math.upenn.edu/History/recog/kadison.html |date=2010-06-19 }} Department of Mathematics, [[University of Pennsylvania]]. Accessed January 12, 2010.</ref>

Kadison was a member of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] (elected in 1996),<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110604020557/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/113810132?pg=vprof&mbr=1001061&returl=http:%2F%2Fwww.nasonline.org%2Fsite%2FDir%2F113810132%3Fpg=srch&view=basic&retmk=search_again_link Kadison, Richard V.], [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]]. Accessed January 12, 2010. Election citation: "Kadison has been the principal figure in the American school of study of operator algebras in Hilbert space since the [[Second World War]] and one of the central leaders of the world development leading to applications in [[quantum field theory]], [[statistical mechanics]], noncommutative geometry, and [[knot theory]]."</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1126/science.272.5263.808 | volume=272 | title=National Academy of Sciences Elects New Members | year=1996 | journal=Science| issue=5263 | pages=808–0 | s2cid=220101739 }}</ref> and a foreign member of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]] (elected 1974)<ref name="guysal"/> and of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>[http://english.dnva.no/c40134/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40147 Academy members list, Mathematical Sciences], [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]. Accessed January 12, 2010.</ref> He was a 1969 [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]].<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=k Guggenheim Fellow list], [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]. Accessed January 12, 2010.</ref>

Kadison was awarded the 1999 [[Steele Prize|Leroy P. Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement]] by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name="penn"/><ref name="ams">{{cite journal | year = 1999 | title = 1999 Steele Prizes | url = https://www.ams.org/notices/199904/comm-steele-prz.pdf | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume = 46 | issue = 4| pages = 457–462 }}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the American Mathematical Society.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref>

==Personal life==
Kadison served as an officer in the merchant marines for several years after 1943.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Murray |first=Arthur Randolph |title=The Smooth Log |publisher=Seaboard Press |year=2006 |isbn=1-59663-762-5 |location=USA}}</ref> He was a skilled gymnast with a specialty in rings, making the 1952 US Olympic Team but later withdrawing due to an injury.<ref name=amsnotices>{{cite journal | last1 = Ge | first1 = Liming| last2 = Jaffe | first2 = Arthur| last3 = Rieffel | first3 = Marc| last4 = Rørdam | first4 = Mikael |date=October 2019 | title = In Memoriam: Richard Kadison (1925–2018) | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume = 66 | issue = 9 | pages = 1453–1463 | doi = 10.1090/noti1949| url = https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201909/rnoti-p1453.pdf | doi-access = free }}</ref> He married Karen M. Holm on June 5, 1956, and they had one son, Lars.<ref name=amsnotices/>

Kadison died after a short illness on August 22, 2018.<ref name="guysal" />
